name: History
facts: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries, with most of today's surviving wall from the Ming dynasty.
Oxford University was already teaching students before the Aztec city of Tenochtitlan was founded.
The shortest war on record, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted less than an hour.
The ancient Egyptians invented one of the earliest known 365-day calendars.
The Eiffel Tower was meant to be temporary and was nearly torn down in 1909.
Napoleon was not unusually short; he was around average height for a Frenchman of his time.
The first recorded Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, in 776 BCE.
The printing press was developed by Johannes Gutenberg around 1440.
The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
India's first general election, held in 1951 to 1952, was the largest election the world had seen at that time.
The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989.
Ancient Egyptians used a form of paper made from the papyrus plant.
The Indus Valley Civilisation had planned cities with drainage systems more than 4,000 years ago.
The Titanic sank on its first voyage in April 1912.
The Roman Empire at its peak stretched from Britain to the Middle East.
Woolly mammoths were still alive on Wrangel Island when the Great Pyramid was being built.
Mahatma Gandhi's Salt March in 1930 covered about 390 kilometres in 24 days.
The first powered flight by the Wright brothers, in 1903, lasted 12 seconds.
Paper money was first widely used in China during the Tang and Song dynasties.
The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States, dedicated in 1886.
Nalanda in ancient India was one of the world's earliest residential universities.
Vikings reached North America around the year 1000, roughly 500 years before Columbus.
The Black Death in the 14th century killed a large share of Europe's population, often estimated at a third or more.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
